memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The LORD said to Moses and Aaron, "When anyone has a swelling or a rash or a shiny spot on their skin that may be a defiling skin disease, they must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest." - Lev 13:1-2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The very first instruction is not about treatment. It is about showing someone.

A swelling, a rash, a shiny spot — none of these was necessarily serious. But the Israelite was not permitted to make that judgement alone in his tent. He had to bring it to the priest. He had to let another set of eyes look at what he might prefer to keep covered.

We resist this instinctively. When something appears in our lives that troubles us — a growing habit, a bitterness we cannot shake, a struggle in our marriage, a doubt we are afraid to voice — our first move is usually concealment. We tell ourselves it is probably nothing. We hope it will fade if we ignore it.

But God's design has always involved bringing things into the light. James tells us to confess our sins to each other and pray for each other, so that we may be healed (Jas 5:16). John writes that if we walk in the light, as He is in the light, we have fellowship with one another (1 John 1:7).

Notice: fellowship comes through the light, not despite it. What we hide isolates us. What we bring into the open, God can heal.

Who is your priest? Who in your life is allowed to look closely?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you currently keeping covered that needs another set of eyes?
2. Do you have someone in your life permitted to speak honestly to you?
3. What makes concealment feel safer than confession?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I confess how quickly I hide what troubles me. Give me courage to bring things into the light, and give me trustworthy people who will look honestly and love me still. Amen.
